pos.personaBrief: Chelsea 2016/17 and Inter 2020/21 were not possession teams: Inter dropped from 61% to 45% during the winning run and hit on the break, while Chelsea controlled games late (FourFourTwo).

pro.personaBrief: Chelsea and Inter went direct to Costa and Lukaku with long balls and quick breaks, though Inter also built from the back through Brozovic and Eriksen.

est.personaBrief: A rehearsed back three with wing-backs and defined roles (3-4-3, 5-3-2), with a striker who links play (Lukaku) and rigid positional structure.

lar.personaBrief: Width comes from wing-backs (Moses, Alonso, Young) in a system with no true wingers, with crosses to Lukaku and a three-man midfield.

blo.personaBrief: A mid-block with a compact back five and zonal-by-ball defending, pressing selectively with strikers; not a gegenpress (reaction to loss is controlled deceleration).

mar.personaBrief: Man-oriented, chain-reaction marking with a back five, though evidence for Chelsea and Inter marking is thin.

pla.personaBrief: Imposes a system but changed it after the Arsenal defeat and adapts to squad and opponent; strongly prepares for rivals.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic and results-first: switched to 3-4-3 to stop conceding, Inter went pragmatic during the winning run, two titles.

sis.personaBrief: System over stars: ruthlessly cleared Icardi, Nainggolan and Perisic for not fitting; reinvented Moses; Costa feud and Terry sidelined.

jog.personaBrief: Physical, intense wing-backs and a target man (Lukaku, Moses, Young); Kante's tackling; runs 8.5km more than United.

bas.personaBrief: Prefers older, experienced, title-winning signings at Inter, though at Chelsea he said he wanted to lower the average age.

lid.personaBrief: Authoritarian and frank: dropped Terry and Ivanovic, feuded with Costa, cleared Icardi; says he tells hard truths.
